statements.text: We know, as has already been noted, AI is so integral to the future, our future success, it cuts across all areas of DOD, but the struggle is, how do we innovate fast enough to keep up with the threat?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on DOD IT, digital developments, and AI for FY2023.

statements.text: In the AI arena, the world requires Congress to step up and lead. [...] Our adversaries have openly stated their desire to dominate the AI field. America must keep up with the pace of AI’s advancement. I look forward to working with members of this task force to educate our colleagues on the urgent need to construct guardrails against emerging threats while also allowing technological innovation to flourish.
statements.venue: Press release on being named to House bipartisan AI Task Force

statements.text:
I look forward to working with members of the bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to educate our colleagues on the urgent need to construct guardrails against emerging threats while also allowing technological innovation to flourish.

Read my full statement below 👇
https://t.co/Omh9OQDXLl

The US should be setting the rules of the road for AI - not the CCP. Read more from my interview with @TIME ⬇️⬇️
https://t.co/VZMHlB3yOT
America cannot sit idly by and watch our adversaries dominate the AI field. I’m proud to serve on the bipartisan AI Task Force as we examine Congress' role in staying ahead. https://t.co/jaBgVp2m1N

I represent an area that’s a long way from Silicon Valley. I’ve got the largest agricultural district east of the Mississippi [River], and we have a lot of challenges that are facing farmers today. Technology can be at least a partial solution. [...] If AI can help us do better weather prediction, that’s going to have massive implications for agriculture.

I think AI is an area that’s going to help us with cybersecurity. I think when there’s so much out there that we need to protect and so many vulnerabilities, I think AI is going to help. But there’s also the other side of that coin: AI is going to enable our adversaries to be much more pervasive in their efforts to try to hack into our systems.
AI is going to be able to help fix that and we can retrain. [...] But I see far more upside and the potential for AI than the downside.

Check out my interview with @fedscoop where we discussed AI-related cybersecurity concerns, AI in agriculture, the private sector’s role in Congress’s AI work and more👇👇
https://t.co/4eUwxPTCFh

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. [...] we now are grappling with this big challenge of how do we take this transformational opportunity that we have that AI is going to present, and what is Congress' role in providing the right guidelines? You know, the guardrails to protect society but also not provide so much, you know, overburdensome regulation that we stifle innovation.
statements.context: House Appropriations subcommittee hearing on the Legislative Branch budget for Fiscal Year 2025, featuring testimony from the Comptroller General.

statements.text: there is a dark side, but there is also a tremendous opportunity. [...] I am interested in how you, as the GAO, are going to be harnessing AI to bring that to bear to assist you. statements.text:
Artificial intelligence is moving fast, and Congress needs to keep pace.

Pleased to work with @JayObernolte on the Great American AI Act discussion draft. This proposal builds on the bipartisan House AI Task Force's work and takes a needed step toward establishing clear rules of the road for advanced AI systems while encouraging innovation.
statements.quoted: Artificial intelligence is changing the way Americans live, work, learn, and compete. Congress needs to do its job in regulating this new technology with a clear national framework that protects Americans while ensuring the United States remains the global leader in AI. Read my op-ed with @RepLoriTrahan here: https://t.co/OffE6R5yTM

statements.text: As a cosponsor of the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, I'm working with @JayObernolte to ensure our regulatory framework keeps pace with sophisticated frontier AI models while fostering American innovation. The bill takes a targeted approach by focusing oversight on the most advanced frontier AI model developers while allowing startups and smaller innovators to build new technologies instead of navigating unnecessary federal red tape.
statements.quoted: Artificial intelligence is moving rapidly, and our regulatory framework must keep pace. Today I introduced the bipartisan FRONTIER Act with @RepLoriTrahan to establish clear national rules of the road for the largest AI developers, including transparency, independent evaluations and reporting of serious incidents. This legislation builds on our Great American AI Act framework to protect Americans from catastrophic risks and ensure the United States remains the global leader in AI. https://t.co/OOMlIDKAxc

statements.text: Keeping America ahead in AI means protecting consumers without holding back innovation. I met with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce’s Chamber Technology Engagement Center to talk about AI, data privacy and keeping American innovators competitive. We must get this right to support American innovation and stay ahead of Communist China.

Cutting edge Frontier AI models are now showing the ability to do things their creators didn’t intend or anticipate.  The implications are serious and must be addressed.   

This week, I participated in a @housescience roundtable with AI industry leaders to take a deeper look at the recent OpenAI/Hugging Face incident and the lessons we need to learn from the rapid advancement of Frontier models. As Congress grapples with establishing proper AI oversight, we must strike the right balance that encourages American innovation while protecting the public. Doing so will be critical to ensuring the AI race isn’t won by authoritarian regimes whose disregard for our Western democratic values could be catastrophic through the abuse or reckless use of this transformational technology.

AI is changing how Americans do business, including how purchases are made.

I met with @ElecTranAssoc to discuss agentic commerce, where AI can make purchases on behalf of consumers and businesses, and what that means for fraud, privacy and accountability. As this technology develops, consumer protections need to keep pace without putting unnecessary roadblocks in the way of American innovation.

Florida Poly continues to put Central Florida at the forefront of emerging technology.

I met with @FLPolyU President Dr. Devin Stephenson and Vice President of Information Technology & CIO Cole Allen to discuss the university’s future and its growing work in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and other cutting-edge fields. We also got a firsthand look at Astro, Florida Poly’s new advanced air mobility police vehicle - the first eVTOL aircraft integrated into a law enforcement agency in the nation.

From the classroom to campus operations, Florida Poly is putting new technology into practice and preparing students to lead in the industries of tomorrow.
